evidence: The 23dc89d diff shows the laws-excise.js header still described 'Part B = an injected self-resume', the four-actions note said 'Both are live; which one runs depends on whether a hosted session is listening', and the TIMING note said 'the launcher runs these actions afterwards' after this PR deleted the launcher and applyRequest. All three were rewritten in 23dc89d.
guidance_note: When a PR deletes a mechanism, grep for the deleted names and concepts (launcher, relaunch, applyRequest, --resume) as well as the removed identifiers, and fix every comment that describes them before pushing.

evidence: The agent confirmed 'Nothing sets LAWS_SWITCH_DIR or LAWS_SWITCH_SESSION after this PR', fixed the comments, and deferred the launcher to xy0.5 (PR #48 shipped it the next day). Deferring was a defensible sequencing call. But the claim that this 'does not break a working live path' sidestepped the relaunch regression, and the agent conceded that in F9. The comment sweep also missed skill-router.sh:341 (F7) and laws-switch:46 (F12). A comment naming a producer that does not exist is a stale-comment problem, not a one-source-of-truth violation.
guidance_note: When a teardown makes a feature unreachable on purpose, record that cost in the design ledger (SEAMS.md) in the same PR, not only in the PR body.

evidence: applyRequest was removed from module.exports in this PR, while switch-request.js still said 'This mirrors what the on-disk path already does in `applyRequest`'. 23dc89d deletes that sentence.
guidance_note: After deleting an exported function, grep the whole tree for its name, comments included.

evidence: The 23dc89d diff removes the line 'the same argv-parsing hazard claude-laws refuses to take on' from bin/laws-switch. That binary was deleted by this PR.
guidance_note: After deleting a file, grep for its basename in comments across the tree.

evidence: This duplicates F2 from the laws-switch side. The agent gave the same reply: comments fixed, launcher deferred to xy0.5. Its claim that bin/laws-switch was 'reworded the same way' was incomplete: the clause 'The launcher owns this directory' stayed and was flagged again as F12.
guidance_note: When promising a reword 'the same way' in named files, re-read every sentence of each named block after editing, not only the anchored line.

evidence: The toRawLines comment 'Three callers ... the two on-disk paths below' went stale when the original PR deleted applyRequest. 23dc89d did not touch it, even though F1's fix said it corrected that file's stale-mechanism comments. 77351a5 dropped the count instead of changing it to two, so the comment no longer restates a fact grep can find.
guidance_note: When fixing stale comments in a file after a deletion, also search the file for counts and enumerations of callers or paths that the deletion changed.

evidence: The agent's F2 fix said skill-router.sh would stop asserting a producer, but the 23dc89d diff of skill-router.sh changes only the retire-craft block. 'The launcher pins its session id up front (claude --session-id)' at line 341 was untouched. The agent admitted 'fixed the wrong paragraph' and swept the whole block in 77351a5.
guidance_note: When a finding says a whole class of claim is false (here, 'a launcher sets these vars'), grep for every sentence that makes that claim instead of editing the instances you remember.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. 77351a5 changed only comments. The silent drop of '--apply' comes from the original commit removing the --apply arm while leaving `args.find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'))`. The fix added parseArgs, which rejects every unknown --option with exit 2. That matches what the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When removing a CLI flag's branch, check what the remaining argv parser now does with that flag; a parser that ignores unknown options turns removed flags into silent no-ops.

evidence: The reviewer re-raised F2's regression: the relaunch path had worked end to end, and the SEAMS.md ledger presented its removal as a pure simplification. The agent conceded 'my prior reply was the narrower answer' and added the disclosure in aeea46c. It cited polishing-by-subtraction only to say that law does not govern a pass that adds a missing fact. 77351a5 never touched SEAMS.md, so this finding is caused by F2's incomplete answer, not by the flagged commit.
guidance_note: When answering a regression report, address the path the reviewer named rather than a different path that is still intact, and record the accepted cost where the next reader will look.

evidence: 77351a5 (F7's fix) changed 'the launcher reads back from the gate' to 'host reads back', but the host never reads `current`. The agent's own check found the only reader is bin/laws-switch:58. The agent admitted 'Correcting a wrong actor to a different wrong actor ... looks freshly verified'.
guidance_note: Before rewriting which component consumes a field, trace that specific field's readers, not just the file's readers.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive here. The agent traced the 'still there to retry' clause to the original commit 5853b93, and the flagged commit aeea46c changed only SEAMS.md. The clause is false for noOffer, because the offer is consumed or malformed. 02b38c8 gives noOffer its own message and imports REFUSED instead of repeating the string.
guidance_note: When adding a reassurance to a user message shared by several failure reasons, check that it holds for every reason that reaches it.

evidence: The F5 reply said bin/laws-switch was reworded so it asserted no producer, but 'The launcher owns this directory' survived, along with the die() text telling users to 'Start the session through the launcher'. The agent fixed both in 02b38c8 and said it was the 'Third round on the same class'.
guidance_note: When fixing a class of false comment, sweep user-facing error strings in the same block too, not only comments.

narrative: This teardown PR deleted the relaunch launcher and left many comments describing it. Round 0 flagged them, plus the unreachable-switch gap. The agent's sweeps were partial three times running: F7, F12 and F6 are leftovers of earlier comment fixes, and F10 is a wrong actor introduced while fixing F7. F9 re-raised F2 because the first answer argued about the live path instead of disclosing the relaunch regression. Round 1 consisted only of fix-caused findings; rounds 2 and 3 also carried real pre-existing bugs (F8, F11).
guidance_observations: The agent claimed a full sweep in round 0 and missed sentences in the very files it named; checking with grep for each deleted concept would have removed round 1.
Replying to a regression report by defending a different code path cost a round; the agent itself later called it 'a dodge'.

evidence:
The format string `'FAIL - %s
'` with the args `"$1
       %s
" "${2:-}"` reuses the format, so each failure prints two FAIL lines with a literal 
. The agent reproduced this, and fed0e35 gives printf the two-%s format.
guidance_note: Run a test harness's failure path once (force one assertion to fail) before relying on its output or its counts.

evidence: Under `set -u`, `${1:-$HOME/.local/bin}` aborts with bash's unbound-variable error when HOME is unset. fed0e35 checks HOME only when no argument is given, dies with a usage message, and adds tests.
guidance_note: Under set -u, give every environment-derived default its own diagnosed check, as the script already does for its other prerequisites.

evidence: The agent showed `env -i /usr/bin/readlink -f /etc/hosts` returning /private/etc/hosts with exit 0 on macOS 26.3, and codesign identified the binary as Apple's stat, not coreutils. It also showed that a mis-resolved PLUGIN_DIR hits the checked 'launcher not found' fallback to stock claude. A portable symlink walker for unsupported macOS versions would be a mode with no use.
This is the same malformed bad() printf as F1. The one fed0e35 change fixes both.
guidance_note: Run a test harness's failure path once (force one assertion to fail) before relying on its output or its counts.

evidence: The entry's own dates (removed 2026-09-05, closed 2026-09-06) give one day, not 'two days'. fed0e35 deletes the duration and leaves the dates as the only statement of the span. The reviewer had offered removal as an option.
guidance_note: Don't restate a span that the dates next to it already determine.

evidence: The original test used PATH=/usr/bin:/bin on the assumption that node is absent, which is false on Debian with the distro nodejs package. fed0e35 builds a NODELESS directory of symlinks and asserts that no node leaked in. The rebuild also surfaced the missing-bash shebang problem.
guidance_note: When a test needs a binary to be absent, build a PATH that guarantees it rather than relying on the host's directory layout.

evidence: The agent showed node rejecting an unknown option with exit 9 before running the script, so an older node with vm.SourceTextModule would fail the probe. The trailing 2>/dev/null already silences the warning, so fed0e35 drops the flag.
guidance_note: Give a capability probe only the flags that the capability itself requires; any extra flag can fail for an unrelated reason.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. fed0e35 touched install-launcher only for HOME and the node flag; the two hardcoded marker literals date from the original commit. A shared sourced file would not work because the token has to appear in the grepped file's first 400 bytes, so a857982 defines it once in the launcher and the installer reads it out.
guidance_note: When the same token must match across two files, write it in one file and have the other read it out, from the first draft.

evidence: The agent first disputed the mechanism using a measurement contaminated by a stray /private/tmp/claude, then conceded in reply 2 that 'your stated mechanism was right and my pushback was wrong'. The `-f && -x` check covers the empty case and also directories and non-executable files. The code dates from the original commit, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Re-run a contradicting measurement from a clean temporary directory before using it to push back on a reviewer.

evidence: The hardcoded /usr/bin/true is absent on NixOS and distroless images. The reviewer's `command -v true` returns the builtin's bare name, as the agent showed. a857982 writes its own stand-in, which also records that it ran. The code is from the original commit, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Have an install-time self-test supply its own stub binary instead of borrowing a system path.

evidence: The 'launcher not found' fallback was the only one with no test. a857982 adds a test that runs a copy without launch.js and asserts the log line, the session start, and that the session is not pinned. The branch dates from the original commit, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a file lists its fallback paths, write one test per listed path before opening the PR.

evidence: The injection is real, but the reviewer's `$(touch ...)` payload is rejected as an arithmetic syntax error; the agent showed `a[$(touch ...)]` does execute. S5 overstates it, since setting an env var already implies running commands. The arithmetic line dates from the original commit, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Never pass an inherited environment value into bash $(( )) without first matching it against an exact numeric shape.

evidence: The README promised 'It never leaves you without a session', but the launcher's marker and depth guards exit 78 with no session, and a comment there calls that 'THE ONE FAILURE THAT CANNOT DEGRADE'. 3be13ce narrows the promise to node problems.
guidance_note: Before writing an absolute guarantee in user docs, check the described code for deliberate exceptions to it.

evidence: install-launcher dies when node is absent (`command -v node ... || die`), which contradicts 'only the launcher needs node'. 3be13ce states three cases: the plugin never needs node, install needs node present, and running degrades without it. The agent noted that the version probe only warns.
guidance_note: When documenting a dependency, check each entry point's own handling of it (install and run separately).

evidence: PROBE_DIR was introduced by a857982, F10's fix replacing /usr/bin/true with a written stand-in. Its two die() paths leave `.claude-laws-probe.$$` behind. c5c9dcc replaces it with a staging directory under a single EXIT trap, combined with F20's fix.
guidance_note: Whenever a fix creates a temporary directory in a user-visible location, set the cleanup trap on the line right after creating it.

evidence: skill-router.sh writes pending.json and lock directories under TMPDIR, as the agent showed by grepping lines 171, 300 and 375, so 'they write nothing' was false. The diff hunk is against base and none of the round-0 or round-1 fix commits shown touch this sentence. The pre-PR text already said 'nothing written'. So the flag reflects original-PR prose, not a fix; the packet does not show exactly which commit wrote it.
guidance_note: Before writing 'writes nothing' in docs, grep the hooks for file writes.

evidence: install-launcher only prints the export line when the target directory is not on PATH, so 'run install-launcher once to put it there' overpromised; bc32f7b rewords it. The die() text appears in the PR's laws-switch diff and is not in any shown fix commit, so it is original-PR text and the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When an error message tells the user what to do, check that the recommended command actually achieves the stated result.

evidence: F12's a857982 fix accepted any run of digits. The agent measured `18446744073709551616` wrapping to depth 1, which bypasses the ceiling, and `08` causing a raw octal error. c5c9dcc accepts only `[0-9]|[1-9][0-9]` instead of adding a separate length check, and the agent called its earlier fix 'half a fix'.
guidance_note: When parsing an untrusted number, accept its canonical bounded shape (no leading zero, bounded length) instead of a character class, so the next stage cannot reinterpret it.

evidence: The eqform case asserted only that no pin was added. The parallel ownid case also asserted the flag passes through unchanged. The test is from the original commit, so the ON-POST-REVIEW flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Give parallel test cases the same assertions, covering both the suppressed effect and the pass-through.

evidence: `printf ... > "$TARGET"` overwrote the working stub before the probe ran, and the probe existed from the first commit. c5c9dcc stages the stub, probes it, then mv's it into place. A test asserts that a failed re-install leaves the original stub byte-identical.
guidance_note: When an installer verifies what it installed, check the candidate before replacing the live file, not after.

evidence: The polluted-stdout scenario is speculative, and the reviewer said so. The real defect is that a malformed id fails the launch where every other bad state degrades. c5c9dcc adds a UUID-shape check that leads to the existing 'could not mint' fallback. The mint code is from the original commit.
guidance_note: Check the shape of a value captured from a subprocess's stdout before passing it on as a flag argument.

evidence: F8's a857982 fix single-sourced the token, but it built MARKER as token plus a hardcoded sentence and matched ownership with `grep -qF "$MARKER"`. Rewording that sentence would make older stubs look foreign. The agent itself said this 'lands directly on the change made for' F8, and c5c9dcc matches on the token alone.
guidance_note: After single-sourcing a token, make every reader match on the token alone, not on prose built around it.

narrative: This PR brought back a setup-only claude-laws launcher and an installer. Rounds 0 and 1 found real defects in the original code (printf harness, HOME, host-layout assumptions, marker duplication, arithmetic injection, docs that overstated guarantees). Every round-1 flag is a false positive because the code predates the named fix. Round 2 had three fix-caused findings: the probe directory leak from F10's fix, the digit-only depth parse from F12's fix (allowing overflow and an octal error), and whole-sentence marker matching left over from F8's fix. The other round-2 findings were original. The agent pushed back once, correctly (macOS readlink -f), and wrongly disputed F9's mechanism with a contaminated measurement before correcting itself.
guidance_observations: Each fix-caused finding came from a fix that introduced new code (a temp dir, a validator, a composed marker) without applying the same scrutiny the fix was about; a mutation or adversarial-input pass on new fix code would have caught F18.
The agent's habit of mutation-testing its fixes repeatedly caught real gaps (the token round-trip test, the exit-0 launcher test) before review did.
